article.title: Forget the RAM crisis: New US tariff proposal could make your next smartphone even more expensive
article.summary: Credit: Ryan Haines / Android Authority TL;DR The US government is considering new tariffs not only on foreign chips but also on consumer electronics like laptops, gaming consoles, and, presumably, smartphones with those chips. Relief may be offered to foreign companies investing in US manufacturing, but constructing facilities takes years, so there may not be room for immediate price relief. Combined with rising costs from AI-driven demand for RAM and storage, these tariffs could soon drive retail prices even higher than current levels. The US government is weighing a sweeping new round of tariffs on semiconductors and finished consumer electronics, a move that could significantly drive up the cost of smartphones, smartwatches, earbuds, and practically everything else with a chip in it. article.title: PayPal Deal Talks End as Advent, Stripe Group Abandons Acquisition Effort
article.summary: A consortium of buyout firm Advent and payment processor Stripe has decided to abandon its pursuit of fintech pioneer PayPal Holdings Inc., a potential deal that would have ranked as one of the biggest-ever leveraged buyouts, according to people familiar with the matter.

article.summary: 數位身分驗證與詐欺防治業者Socure併購AI代理平臺Fravity，並完成新一輪募資，公司估值提高至52億美元。路透社披露，本輪募資金額為1.56億美元。

article.title: Anthropic's new hardware standard lets AI agents control the physical world
article.summary: For all the interest in and uptake of agentic AI systems over the past year or so , the world of automated AI has thus far been primarily limited to text, images, code, and other data and actions that take place inside a computer. Anthropic is now aiming to change that somewhat with what it's calling the Model Hardware Standard (MHS), a set of standardized drivers designed to let AI agents easily interface with and control arbitrary devices. For now, the "research preview" of the MHS effort is being sold mainly as a way to help scientists streamline the arduous process of creating the custom software integrations that are often needed to get disparate components of an experiment working in concert. MHS can provide a common interface and common format for data sharing between these devices,

article.title: Google Photos could soon let you take a shortcut straight to your favorite media
article.summary: TL;DR Google Photos version 7.90 includes an unreleased feature that could let you pin custom shortcuts to the Collections tab. In testing, long-pressing folders, albums, or people allowed pinning them to a horizontal scrolling bar at the top of the app. A dedicated Edit menu could let you reorder pinned items or browse organized library categories to customize your view. When Google replaced the classic Library view with the updated Collections tab, it promised a cleaner way to organize media. However, the top of the screen has remained largely rigid, with Google automatically and unilaterally deciding which shortcuts to highlight while burying your most-used folders. article.title: Google Search's AI Mode can now track flight prices and book hotels for you
article.summary: Today Google is giving its AI Mode the ability to track flight prices for you. This is basically the existing Google Flights feature, but brought into AI Mode in Google Search. You can set up price alerts as you chat. You can also just use AI Mode like Google Flights now, simply describing where and when you want to fly and it will show you the best options available from over 300 partner airlines and travel sites.
